subject: Re: Dedicated capacity performance validation & SLOs
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Sam Jenkins <sam.jenkins@acmeretail.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@acmeretail.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Apr 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity performance validation — post-call recap & next steps

Hi Sam / Priya — great conversation earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can scope the dedicated capacity validation: 

Recap of requirements from today
- Latency SLOs: p95 <= 200ms (batch size 1, streaming enabled for partial tokens)
- Throughput target: sustained 500 QPS at 1k token avg sequence length for inference requests
- Concurrency: support 40 concurrent streams with smooth tail latency
- Model: Llama2-70B fine-tuned (quantized FP16 + some INT8 experiments expected)
- Streaming: required (clients expect token-by-token streaming within 30–50ms of generation)

What we'll validate
- GPU comparisons (A100 40GB vs H100 80GB vs A10G) for your model/quantization mix
- Reserved throughput sizing to hit p95 SLO under typical workload patterns (burst tolerance and steady state)
- Concurrency shaping and streaming latency measurements (end-to-end from request to first token)
- Failure/fallback behavior: what happens when reserved pool is saturated (fallback to compatible model variant)

Proposed plan & timeline
1) You share a representative test corpus (200–500 sample prompts) and expected response length distribution (est. tokens).
2) Redwood spins up dedicated pools (3 configs) and runs a benchmark matrix over 2 business days.
3) We deliver a results matrix + recommended reserved throughput + cost estimates.

Attachments: preliminary benchmark matrix and a short config proposal (see attachments).

Immediate ask from you: please confirm the sample prompts, and whether you can provide a short test key with access to a dev workspace (or we can run with sanitized sample data). Also let us know any procurement/contract blockers (MSA, NDA).

Thanks,
Marissa
Sr. Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0193

—
Attachment stubs referenced: dedicated-config-proposal.pdf (proposal), redwood-benchmark-matrix.xlsx (matrix template)

From: Sam Jenkins <sam.jenkins@acmeretail.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@acmeretail.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity performance validation — post-call recap & next steps

Thanks Marissa — that recap looks spot on. A few clarifications from our side: 

- We can commit to the 200ms p95 target for user-facing web actions; for background batch jobs p95 can be higher.
- Model specifics: Llama2-70B fine-tuned with a pointer-generator head. We'll likely want to run INT8/FP16 comparisons.
- Streaming: yes, streaming is required. Our front-end expects the first token within 50ms of generation start under normal conditions.
- Typical request profile: 70% short prompts (~128 tokens), 25% medium (512 tokens), 5% long (1024 tokens).
- Peak concurrency window: 40–60 concurrent users for the pilot; target sustained concurrency is 40.

We can share 300 sample prompts (sanitized) by EOD tomorrow. We prefer H100 if you can demonstrate meaningful latency/throughput gains for our workload — cost delta is OK if ROI is clear.

Procurement: we have the standard vendor onboarding and MSA review — should be fine but expect legal to ask for SOC2 evidence and a standard SLA.

—Sam
Sam Jenkins
Director, AI Products | Acme Retail
sam.jenkins@acmeretail.com

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Sam Jenkins <sam.jenkins@acmeretail.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@acmeretail.com>

Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity performance validation — post-call recap & next steps

Hi Sam / Priya — thanks for the details; that's very helpful. Technical plan from Redwood SRE/Performance team: 

Planned benchmark matrix (we'll run each cell for steady-state + short burst tests)
- GPUs: H100 (80GB), A100 (40GB), A10G (24GB)
- Model variants: full FP16, quantized INT8, KV-cache warm vs cold
- Scenarios: single-request latency (streaming first token latency), sustained throughput (QPS with target p50/p95), concurrency ramp (0 -> 60 users)
- Metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, first-token streaming latency, tokens/sec, GPU utilization, memory footprint, cost per 1M tokens

Experiment details we need from you:
- 300 sanitized prompts + expected avg response tokens (or distribution you mentioned)
- Any ensemble/penalties or decoding knobs you run in prod (top_k, top_p, temperature)
- Preferred schedule for running the tests (we're suggesting Fri 16 Apr — low traffic window for us)

Deliverables
- Raw benchmark results (CSV), summarized matrix (PDF) with recommended reserved throughput and pool sizing per GPU type, cost delta table, and suggested canary rollout plan for Dedicated capacity.

Note on streaming measurement: we'll validate end-to-end from your client when possible — if you can provide a dev key and a test client endpoint we can measure real client-perceived first-token latency. Otherwise we'll run server-side emulation with header timings.

I've attached the benchmark matrix template; we'll populate it and share interim results during the run.

Cheers,
Aditya Rao
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.com

- Procurement: we'll surface SOC2 documentation and the SLA template in the same HubSpot deal; legal usually signs MSA + SOW before Dedicated starts — I'll send the DocuSign link this afternoon.
- Data access: please upload the sanitized prompts to the shared Drive folder (link in related_links) or grant a short-lived S3 key; we'll confirm receipt and checksum before starting.
- Schedule: we can start the runs on Fri 16 Apr at 09:00 PT if that still works for you — that gives us Friday + Monday to complete the matrix and produce interim results by EOD Mon 19 Apr.

I'll loop Rafael from Solutions to help with the onboarding and to set up the dev key for client-side streaming tests. Rafael — can you take point on the dev key creation and client test harness?

Sam/Priya — thanks again, and we should be able to provide clear sizing guidance (reserved throughput and recommended GPU class) after the run.

Best,
